context.objective: Add employee profile photos to the existing employee portal with employee upload, manager viewing, and policy-based HR removal.
context.current_task: Review the focused requirements while preserving supplied unknowns and storage implementation neutrality.
in_scope: Employee upload of their own JPG or PNG profile photo
HR removal when a photo violates company policy
actors: Employee — can upload their own JPG or PNG profile photo (SUPPORTED)
Employee's manager — can view the employee's photo (SUPPORTED)
HR — can remove a photo when it violates company policy (SUPPORTED)
systems: Existing employee portal — already authenticates employees, managers, and HR (SUPPORTED)
Profile-photo storage implementation — not selected and constrained to remain technology-neutral in this exercise (SUPPORTED)
authoritative_sources: Project opening and twelve supported facts supplied for the focused conformance exercise
confirmed_business_rules: Employees can upload JPG or PNG profile photos.
Maximum profile-photo file size is 5 MB.
The employee's manager can view the photo.
HR can remove a photo if it violates company policy.
The existing portal already authenticates employees, managers, and HR.
No storage implementation has been selected.
Storage technology must remain implementation-neutral for this requirements exercise.
derived_facts: Photo format and file size must be available to the rule evaluator because the supported type and size rules cannot be evaluated without them.
constraints: Storage technology must remain implementation-neutral for this requirements exercise.
File type and size rules must not be converted into an unsupported rejection, blocking, deletion, or transformation consequence.
terminology: Employee's manager — the manager related to the employee whose photo is being viewed.
Company policy violation — the supplied condition under which HR can remove a photo; policy content and adjudication are not defined by the evidence.

decisions: Use QUICK GAL mode for the narrow, supplied profile-photo capability and focused evidence review.
Preserve resizing/compression, EXIF handling, removal notifications, audit history, and employee self-deletion as UNKNOWN without creating questions or decision debt.
Treat storage technology neutrality as an in-scope constraint rather than an out-of-scope declaration.
Do not create blocking decision debt for eventual implementation choices that do not prevent meaningful progression on the established requirements.
